_comment: The DIVERGENCE LEDGER for the ODRE decision-agreement lane (bead sq-i6du2.8).
Every sparq-vs-ODRE disagreement the run observes must match exactly one entry here or
the run FAILS with exit 3 (unclassified divergence). An entry is a pre-registered,
sourced explanation — not a mute. The three classes are the ones the bead fixes:
mapping-gap        the two systems were not asked the same question: the divergence
is attributable to the input mapping or to a capability one side
semantics-gap      both systems read the same policy and disagree about what ODRL
MEANS; a documented, defensible difference of reading.
implementation-bug neither of the above: one implementation does not do what its own
`evidence` states HOW the entry is justified and is the honesty hinge:
source-read  derived from reading the pinned implementation's source; PREDICTED, not
yet confirmed by a run on this box.
observed     confirmed by a recorded run of this lane (name the run).
A source-read entry is a hypothesis. The report labels it as such, and no claim about
either system's correctness is made from it.

entries.title: ODRE has no request model: assignee/target/action are not consulted when selecting rules
entries.source: pyodre 1.0.6 pyodre/odre.py: `enforce(self, policy, format, interpolations)` takes no request; `_rules` selects every odrl:permission/prohibition/obligation object and `_constraints`/`_action` never read odrl:assignee or odrl:target.
entries.note: This is why the lane also runs the `projected` encoding, where the harness performs request binding before handing the policy to ODRE. A divergence of this shape under `projected` is NOT covered by this entry and will fail the run.

entries.title: Constraints linked through odrl:constraint are not reached by ODRE's constraint query, so a constrained rule fires unconstrained
entries.source: pyodre 1.0.6 pyodre/odre.py `_constraints` selects `<rule> odrl:operator ?op ; odrl:leftOperand ?l ; odrl:rightOperand ?r` — constraint properties directly on the RULE node. ODRL 2.2 (W3C REC, sec. 2.5) attaches them to a separate node via odrl:constraint, which that pattern does not reach; `decision = len(constraints_set) == 0` then admits the rule.
entries.note: Classified implementation-bug rather than semantics-gap because it diverges from the ODRL Recommendation's own encoding, not from a defensible alternative reading of it. Scoped to the `standard` encoding: the `odre-native` encoding inlines the constraints precisely so this does not silently dominate the study. UNCONFIRMED until a run with pyodre installed observes it — `evidence: source-read`.

entries.title: ODRE evaluates a prohibition as an enforceable rule; sparq applies deny-overrides
entries.source: pyodre 1.0.6 pyodre/odre.py `_rules` VALUES-binds odrl:permission, odrl:obligation AND odrl:prohibition into one rule list and adds each satisfied rule's action to the usage decision — a prohibition contributes positively. sparq-policy applies deny-overrides (crates/sparq-policy/src/eval.rs `evaluate` step 1), the fail-closed side and the documented divergence from ODRL's unset-`odrl:conflict` default (crates/sparq-policy/README.md, issue #1375).
entries.note: A genuine difference of reading on both sides: neither is 'correct' here, and this lane does not adjudicate. It records that a policy's prohibitions change the decision in sparq and do not in ODRE.

entries.title: For a rule carrying several odrl:action values, ODRE reports an arbitrary one
entries.source: pyodre 1.0.6 pyodre/odre.py `_action` returns `[str(row.action) for row in graph.query(...)][0]` — the first row of an UNORDERED SPARQL result set. A rule granting Read+Write+Control therefore contributes exactly one of them to the usage decision, chosen non-deterministically (rdflib result order varies with PYTHONHASHSEED).
entries.note: Pre-registered as a flake guard as much as a finding: without it, a run in which the arbitrary pick happens to miss the requested action would surface as an unexplained sparq-allow/ODRE-deny. run.sh pins PYTHONHASHSEED to make a run reproducible; that pins the symptom, not the cause. Not applicable to `projected`, where the harness filters each bound rule down to the requested action.

entries.title: ODRE's interpreter refuses any URI outside its prefix map
entries.source: pyodre 1.0.6 pyodre/python_interpreter.py `__interpreted_function_mappings` raises for any URI not matching a registered prefix (odrl / xsd / odre-time / odre-demo by default).
entries.note: The harness pre-registers the sparq acl action namespace through ODRE's own documented `add_prefix_mapping` extension point, so this should be residual — e.g. an IRI-valued right operand from a corpus vocabulary. A refusal is recorded as a mapping gap, never coerced into a decision.
